title: Classic Problems I: Design Decisions
summary: Parking lot, vending machine, games and caches. The decisions that separate a hire from a no-hire.

questions.q: In a parking lot, how should you model the rule "bikes fit anywhere, cars need medium+, trucks need large"?
options: `class Car extends Vehicle` with an overridden `canPark(Spot)` in every subclass
Give each vehicle type a minimum spot size, and say a spot fits if `spot.size ≥ type.minSize`, with ordered enums
A nested `switch` inside `ParkingLot.park`
Separate `BikeParkingLot`, `CarParkingLot` and `TruckParkingLot` classes
questions.explain: The rule is data, not behaviour. An ordered enum comparison is short and correct, and a new type is one enum constant.

questions.q: Two entry gates call `park()` at the same instant and both pick spot F1-M1. What's the simplest correct fix for a single lot?
options: Make `Spot.isFree()` `volatile`
Run the find-free-spot and occupy steps inside one critical section (a lock on the lot), firing events after releasing it
Retry if the spot turns out to be taken
Give each gate its own set of spots
questions.explain: Selection plus occupation is a check-then-act. One short lock is simple and obviously correct. Mention finer granularity as an optimisation.

questions.q: In the vending machine, a user selects a product that costs more than the inserted balance. What should happen?
options: Refund the balance and go back to IDLE
Fail with an insufficient-funds error, keeping the HAS_MONEY state and the balance unchanged
Dispense the product and record a debt
Throw and reset the machine
questions.explain: A failed operation shouldn't change state. The user may insert another coin.

questions.q: Why do LRU cache solutions use sentinel head and tail nodes?
options: To store the capacity
They remove null checks for the first and last element, so insert and unlink are always the same four pointer updates
Java requires them
They make the cache thread-safe
questions.explain: Sentinels remove the edge cases, so you write less code with fewer bugs, which matters under time pressure.

questions.q: How do you make the N×N tic-tac-toe win check O(1) per move?
options: Scan the row, column and both diagonals after each move
Keep per-row, per-column and two diagonal counters (+1 for X, −1 for O). A win is when one of the touched counters reaches ±N
Precompute all winning lines and check every one
Use a hash of the board
questions.explain: Each move touches at most 4 counters. Scanning is O(N), which is fine to mention first, but the interviewer usually wants the counters.

questions.q: Snake & ladder tests need deterministic games. What's the cleanest design?
options: Seed `Math.random()` globally in tests
Inject a `Dice` interface into the game. Tests pass a scripted sequence, and production uses a random implementation
Make `rollDice()` protected and override it in a test subclass
Add a `debug` flag that fixes rolls
questions.explain: Dependency injection of randomness, just like the clock. A subclass override also works, but it couples tests to internals.

questions.q: In chess, where should the movement rules live?
options: In `Board.isValidMove()`, with a switch on piece type
In each piece (polymorphic `candidateMoves(board, from)`), while the board only answers occupancy questions. Legality (not leaving your king in check) is checked by the game
In the `Player` class
In a static `Rules` utility
questions.explain: Pieces know how they move, and the board knows where things are. A two-phase check keeps the pieces simple.

questions.q: The logging framework has a logger at INFO and a file handler at DEBUG. A `debug()` call…
options: Is written to the file because the handler accepts DEBUG
Is dropped by the logger before it reaches any handler
Throws an exception
Is buffered until the level changes
questions.explain: Both filters apply, and the logger's check comes first. It's also the cheap one, which matters for performance.

questions.q: Composite file system: `size("/home")` must include every nested file. What's the idiomatic implementation?
options: Keep a running total in a global map
`Directory.size()` sums `child.size()` over its children, which recurses naturally because files and directories share the `Node` interface
Walk a flat list of all paths and filter by prefix
Cache sizes in each file
questions.explain: That's what Composite is for. Mention caching sizes with invalidation as an optimisation for very large trees.

questions.q: Interviewer: "Now support electric cars that need charging spots." Which answer shows your parking-lot design was right?
options: "I'll add an `isElectric` flag and an `if` in park()."
"I'll add an EV spot capability and an `EvAwareSpotSelector` strategy that prefers charging spots for EVs. `ParkingLot` itself doesn't change."
"I'd need to redesign the Spot hierarchy."
"Create a separate EV parking lot class."
questions.explain: Extensions should land in the abstraction you introduced for variation. Point at the class you'd add.
